exposure: birth mother beneficiary type (sponsor, dependent spouse, other)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 632,565 live births identified from January 2016 through December 2021 among infants born to United States military-connected families (TRICARE beneficiaries).
finding: The study characterized 632,565 live births to US military-connected families from 2016-2021, detailing parental demographics, military characteristics, and the prevalence of adverse outcomes including cesarean delivery (28.2%), preterm birth (7.3%), low birthweight (5.2%), and major birth defects (3.4%).
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was reported for 28.2% of births, and all measured adverse outcomes, including cesarean delivery, were more likely to occur at civilian versus military hospitals.
